dialogue:
Speaker1: Let's take them to the guillotine, seriously.
Speaker2: That'd be kinda unfair if they have nobles but just get rid of the king.
Speaker1: Can't we just roll in with the army, wipe them out, and take their stuff?
Speaker2: Even without a monarchy, if there's a state, someone's still gonna end up on top.

Speaker1: Who in their right mind would give up custody over a cat?
Speaker2: So the husband tried to get her pregnant knowing what she’s like? Seems like guys end up with similar types too.
Speaker1: Feels like the world’s gone weird. Maybe we should just hunt down these cat moms like they did in medieval Europe.
Speaker2: Seems like there are a ton of cat moms, but no cat dads around, so it kinda feels like mental issues are just a thing for women.
Speaker1: Still, to give up custody and get a divorce? The guy better hold on tight to that lifeline he’s been given.

Speaker1: Haha, it's hilarious how the writer's totally trashing it, saying it's boring like they’re gonna get called out.
Speaker2: No idea where that scratch came from. You don't think it got scratched 'cause someone said something dumb about harassment, right?
Speaker1: I think it’s because of the stuff they usually say.
Speaker2: It's hilarious that there are yellow monkeys complaining about PC. You guys are the ones benefiting from it, anyway.

Speaker1: It's really sad when someone approaches you first, but you can't even act like a decent person 'cause you're single.
Speaker2: For real, even if a guy's not that good-looking, if he's got a great personality, confidence, and a good sense of humor, I can't help but feel inferior.
Speaker1: Honestly, unless you're like a total heartthrob, if you ain't got a funny personality, I don't think girls find you attractive.
Speaker2: I feel like even if you're quiet, having at least one thing you're good at can be attractive, but Korean girls really seem to care too much about being funny.

Speaker1: This airline's got a ton of issues, for real.
Speaker2: I think comments like this are really low-level. Have you ever been on a plane? The exit row seats are agreed upon and are wider and more comfortable than other seats.
Speaker1: Sounds like you’re just deflecting; maybe take a look in the mirror first.
Speaker2: I think it’s best if I just chill at home.

Speaker1: Isn't it a real win for humanity when you see how hard I've worked since my early 20s to save this much?
Speaker2: It's impressive you saved that much, but you gotta find other ways to leverage that money.
Speaker1: What are you talking about? Even salary workers like you won't save a dime no matter how hard you try.
Speaker2: Don’t you know about investing in stocks or crypto? That could totally turn your life around.

Speaker1: Heard a college girl jumped out of a cab and died 'cause the driver took a weird route.
Speaker2: Heard that taxi driver got acquitted. The passenger asked for the destination twice, but he didn’t answer.
Speaker1: They said he has an ear problem. He hasn’t been able to drive for years, so it’s been tough for him financially.
Speaker2: Is it really about making a living when someone lost their life? They must've been so scared to jump out.
Speaker1: It's just excessive safety anxiety, right? Is the driver really at fault? I think the society that creates all this fear is the real problem.

Speaker1: Wow, how much work did you do to wear down your fingerprints?
Speaker2: I dedicated 40 years for copyright.
Speaker1: Why try to make someone a criminal over this?
Speaker2: Wait, you really think I just did spiral binding for 40 years? That’s just a dumb thing to say.

Speaker1: Wait, are those app nerds still carrying around transit cards?
Speaker2: Wait, what do you mean? They were praising Apple all this time?
Speaker1: Why on earth would anyone use such a weird phone?
Speaker2: They say it’ll still be going on in 2025. Such a bunch of pretentious app fanboys.

Speaker1: Gonna be late tonight 'cause of a work dinner. Eating with the crew.
Speaker2: What’s up with another dinner meeting today? Are you all just too busy eating instead of working?
Speaker1: What are you talking about? I’m working my butt off here. Can’t you say anything else to your husband?
Speaker2: Got it, just eat and come home early.
Speaker1: There's an old saying that even the finest feast tastes like dirt. I'm not going because I want to, so please understand.

Speaker1: Are you still living like that, even getting free meals as you get older?
Speaker1: Guess you’re still living that same old bottom-of-the-barrel life, huh?
Speaker1: Whatever, go throw some bricks around.
Speaker2: Guess it feels heavy coming from someone who's been hauling bricks their whole life.

Speaker1: Why am I only seeing those creepy guys on my Insta feed lately?
Speaker2: It's 'cause their legs are super short.
Speaker1: I totally agree. Those pants are so ugly, but the confidence to wear them is impressive.
Speaker2: Not a good vibe seeing those guys in Hongdae.

Speaker1: I heard Koreans have an average IQ of 105, while Southeast Asia's is around 80.
Speaker2: Yeah, maybe some of your ancestors mixed in with them? Ask your mom.

Speaker1: No need to go far; remember that leak from the last time?
Speaker1: Can't even say a word of protest in this situation.
Speaker2: If they're spying on their own people, what's the big deal?
Speaker1: That's a problem, and that's a problem too, right, Senshing?
Speaker2: China's always doing stuff like that too, right?

Speaker1: I just don’t get why people lie about buying stuff from abroad.
Speaker2: That girl character in the drama has some real mental issues.
Speaker1: What’s up with saying she got a job somewhere else when no one even asked?
Speaker2: That's just the setup, acting like she knows.

Speaker1: I saw that the agency of the actor who recently committed suicide is gonna sue the haters.
Speaker2: It seems like they've crossed a line. How can they not realize that words can lead to someone's death?
Speaker1: Anyone can file a lawsuit, but whether there'll be any punishment is a whole different story.
Speaker2: Watching fights, online or offline, is always entertaining.

Speaker1: Why hiking, of all things?
Speaker2: It's because you see a person's true nature when you're pushed to the limit, physically and mentally, while hiking.
Speaker1: It was wild the first time I went hiking with my ex. She was complaining about everything—how hard it was, her legs hurt, just all kinds of annoying stuff.
Speaker2: It's a way to see if she's the type to bail as soon as a guy hits a rough patch financially or otherwise.

Speaker1: There's not a single nerdy element since it's picked by those guys.
Speaker2: Baldur's Gate is a game that Americans are gonna love.
Speaker1: Keep in mind, the opinions of weebs are totally worthless and meaningless.
Speaker2: Looks like Korean otakus are gonna go rate-bomb if their fave's ranking is low.

Speaker1: Having a narcissist friend is just exhausting and uncomfortable, honestly.
Speaker2: Yeah, if they don't even realize they're a narcissist, there's not much you can do.
Speaker1: Ignoring is the best move, but I keep forgetting.
Speaker2: Gotta push back hard against those cowardly people who can't even face facts.
Speaker1: Yeah, gotta either hit 'em with facts or just keep quiet.

Speaker1: I'm so excited I can't sleep.
Speaker2: Just chill for now and plan some fun stuff to do.
Speaker1: I won't be able to have too much fun since we'll be video calling every night, but just having some freedom feels great.
Speaker2: Don’t let your guard down till the end. Even a moment of laughter could shatter everything, so be careful.
Speaker1: For sure. One slip-up and it could get rough. You know that better than anyone.
Speaker2: For sure. You're quite the lady. You must've totally killed Admiral Yi Sun-sin in a past life.

Speaker1: I totally get where the girl’s coming from.
Speaker2: Wait, so it’s the guy’s fault? The person cheating is the one with the problem, not the guy.
Speaker1: Dude's looks scream premature ejaculation. Bet he finishes in like 3 seconds.
Speaker2: Talking to you feels like it’s messing with my character. Better to just avoid you.

Speaker1: The airport's crowded just 'cause all the foreign workers are heading home for the long holiday.
Speaker2: Korean tourists are also increasing every year.
Speaker1: Are all the Chinese immigrants bailing?
Speaker2: Did you know that in 2024, the top tourists visiting Japan will be Koreans?

Speaker1: I can totally make sure no one gets bedsores if you cut the patient load to 5 per nurse.
Speaker2: I don't think it'll be easy with people making ridiculous claims about illegal medical practices.
Speaker1: Improving conditions is a priority, and we need legal protection for the tasks we handle instead of doctors.
Speaker2: They’ve been getting nurses to handle all the annoying stuff for cheap, but once the nursing law gets revised, that’ll change. So, it’s all about the money for them.

Speaker1: I heard there's a theory that you can live healthily just by breathing, and it's trending in the U.S.
Speaker2: Can people really say that in a place like the U.S.? Those folks don’t do fasting anyway.
Speaker1: I heard some people even died trying to follow that.
Speaker2: It's pretty wild how strong human will is, seeing people actually believe that nonsense and end up dying from it.

Speaker1: Feels like the older I get, the more I’m shelling out for these events. My salary isn’t going up, but the invites just keep coming.
Speaker2: So I’m not doing gifts, but I’m trying to help out with funerals. But it seems like a lot of people pass away in winter, which is tough.

Speaker1: Being an adult means acting like one; just being older doesn't make you an adult.
Speaker2: Aren't you just being a hypocrite, though?
Speaker1: Just 'cause you're older doesn't mean you're a good adult. If you mess up, you get called out.
Speaker2: I gotta make sure I don’t end up like that.

Speaker1: Did you see their face today? They really went all out on the makeup.
Speaker2: She's known for her makeup skills, though.
Speaker1: Changing your looks ain't easy.
Speaker2: It's kinda sad now.

Speaker1: These are the drawings I made this year. What do you think? Can’t show more because of the size limit.
Speaker2: You should be thankful for AI. Without it, you’d probably just be a struggling artist who can’t draw.
Speaker1: That's harsh. People like you hold back those who could actually improve.
Speaker2: You can't even get perspective right, can't draw human figures properly, and your compositions are just flat shapes, so you should probably just quit.

Speaker1: Isn't my wife Annamie just awesome? She can rock a tracksuit and slippers like nobody's business.
Speaker2: Guess she looks cute to him, but she's just a regular mom, really.
Speaker1: With an eye like that, it’s no wonder you’re still single.

Speaker1: It might be normal to think living like that looks messy, but openly putting someone down is just not cool.
Speaker2: Thinking that way at all isn’t normal. Treating everyone with low pay and education like losers is just messed up.
Speaker1: Still, you don’t just say that. Thinking it’s okay to blurt out whatever just because it’s true shows a lack of basic education, no matter who you are.
Speaker2: It's messed up to have bad thoughts about someone just doing their thing on the street.

Speaker1: Wow, only one person applied for 188 spots in OB-GYN? That's a big deal.
Speaker2: Yeah, with a birth rate of 0.7%, I get it.
Speaker1: I heard some places in Gangwon do give a lot of money for having kids.
Speaker2: Even if you have kids, it’s tough to make a living without jobs.
Speaker1: I think it's a serious issue that more women are going to plastic surgery than to obstetrics these days.
Speaker2: Is it really the women's fault? There's a bigger issue in society.

Speaker1: What I’ve noticed working at a factory anyone can get into is that the mental age is pretty low.
Speaker2: So just because they're older, they think they're special?
Speaker1: It's like they've got arrogance and pride ingrained in them.
Speaker2: I'm so sick of you being jealous just 'cause I got my certification.

Speaker1: What’s with all this anti-kid stuff? Took my kid to a restaurant and had the wildest time.
Speaker2: Kids are so precious these days!
Speaker1: For real. Kids might run around and be loud sometimes, but people act like it's the end of the world.
Speaker2: Your kid is kinda special, though. He's got a ton of energy.

Speaker1: I feel like alcoholism is a disease that only ends in death. I had to pick my dad up from the police station yesterday.
Speaker2: That sounds really tough.
Speaker1: When he drinks, he just goes around hitting people. I even went to apologize to the victim yesterday.
Speaker2: Maybe it's better to cut him off? How long are you gonna keep watching this? Your dad's really hopeless.
Speaker1: I wish he’d just go somewhere and quietly die.
Speaker2: I guess you're saying that 'cause it's so tough. Hang in there.

Speaker1: Seems like kids these days just stare at their phones and don’t know how to look people in the eye.
Speaker2: I guess it's 'cause they just text or use their phones even when they meet up.
Speaker1: Seems like they’ve got no patience and don’t know how to do much since they’re always glued to their phones.
Speaker2: And they wanna do everything super fast, which is a problem.

Speaker1: It's hilarious how they're just forcing me to say pork belly is good while making me eat it.
Speaker2: I guess that cuts down the wait time and lets you eat faster, huh?
Speaker1: So it seems like the restaurant owner really likes guys.
Speaker2: Now that I'm in my 30s, I'm kinda craving that spicy pork I loved in my 20s.

Speaker1: To keep your skin good, avoid booze and cigs, use sunscreen, eat healthy, and get enough sleep.
Speaker2: I'm 50, but I drink every day and still get told I look young everywhere I go.
Speaker1: I swear, people like you who think they're young are kinda delusional. To a 20-something, you just look like any other old dude.
Speaker2: You should start using sunscreen before you get any older. But hey, if you're too broke to buy sunscreen, might as well not have kids, right?

Speaker1: You just gotta accept that no matter how pretty a woman is, time's gonna age her and make her less attractive. It's just nature's law, man.
Speaker2: I get it in my head, but even if I say I accept and love it, my heart just doesn't follow. What should I do?
Speaker1: So you couldn't stick to your principles and ended up cheating with a young college girl? That's just sad...
Speaker2: You'd act the same way if you were in that situation. Would you really feel love looking at those wrinkles?

Speaker1: Stop hoarding food at home and get a part-time job or something.
Speaker2: Hope you get hit by a drunk driver while walking and end up on the moon.
Speaker1: Looking in the mirror, your belly's the real tragedy.
Speaker2: At first, you acted like you had some logic, but now you're just being petty.

Speaker1: But can that friend handle social life?
Speaker2: I think people like that need some financial therapy.
Speaker1: Looks like that kid's gotten caught up in some far-right stuff and can't see things clearly.
Speaker2: For real, they really wanna go to the bakery.

Speaker1: I get that some people are grossed out, but I can't understand the boycotting or trashing the company.
Speaker2: Whoa, your mindset is even scarier. You go eat a lot.
Speaker1: How long do you think the typical Korean will stick to it? If only the interest rates were lower, I would’ve jumped in at the bottom. What a bummer.
Speaker2: What a disgusting person. They say 758 people got caught in the dough mixer and got hurt or died over the past 5 years...

Speaker1: I mean, there’s no right answer, but I feel like one day they might get it right or get stabbed.
Speaker2: Sounds exhausting... Those types of people probably went through some serious issues or family drama.
Speaker1: I don’t get why they’d go out of their way to fight when just the obvious nonsense is so common.
Speaker2: Some people dodge the crap, but others just step in it and get their feet dirty.

Speaker1: The inside's got fleece, so it's warm. The hat's the only downside, though.
Speaker2: What's wrong with the hat?
Speaker1: That's just hilarious.
Speaker2: But you keep saying the hat's fine.

Speaker1: That's why they call the 9th grade a godsend; I think it's a million times better than getting into a big company.
Speaker2: That makes no sense; working a decade in a big company and getting fired won't even match a 9-grade lifetime income.
Speaker1: Shut up, 9-gong is the best.
Speaker2: The old 9th-grade civil servant was legit. My wife supported me, and the pension was great. But what about the 9th-grade now? It's tough to get married, the pension's shrinking, and being a civil servant isn't that great.

Speaker1: I realized none of my old coworkers are rooting for me after leaving to start my own business.
Speaker2: Of course. If you go out and do well, the ones left behind will feel like they failed.
Speaker1: They need me to struggle so they can feel superior and maybe buy me a meal or something.
Speaker2: Aside from family, no one’s really rooting for you. Your success will just make others jealous.
Speaker1: I’m gonna succeed even if it kills me, just so I don’t have to see that. I’ll make everyone bow their heads in front of me.

Speaker1: Looks like you’ve got a crappy phone or computer.
Speaker2: Guess you really like crap since your brain's full of it.
Speaker1: It's tough for idiots, but I'm good.
Speaker2: What kind of bad smartphone, computer, or internet connection lags even on maps these days?

Speaker1: That claim that habits are determined by DNA makes no sense, so why are you saying that?
Speaker2: So that's why they experimented with identical twins, but seriously, how far are you planning to run from this?
Speaker1: People like you, who think everything's true just because there's research, can live your whole life being fooled.
Speaker2: Then provide more reliable info or explain it logically.

Speaker1: Should've nailed it back then, kinda bummed.
Speaker2: For real, that would've been so satisfying. I really didn't want to see that.
Speaker1: It's hilarious how he sucks up to every senior and still messes things up for the juniors, then ends up in jail.
Speaker2: It’s clear to everyone that not handling it back then was a huge mistake.

Speaker1: I don’t think I can make it to work today, my stomach’s acting up. Sorry!
Speaker2: Again? You bailed last week too and made things a hassle. What’s up with that?
Speaker1: But what can I do if I'm in pain? I just have a weak stomach.
Speaker2: If you're that weak, you shouldn't be working. Can't be a burden at someone else's job.
Speaker1: I think you're being a bit harsh on someone who's sick, even if you're the boss.
Speaker2: No need to work for a boss like that. Starting tomorrow, anyone feeling sick should just stay home.

Speaker1: Back in the day, the Halcas in front of Pagoda was five grand an hour, so I used to go there all the time.
Speaker2: I miss the old days.

Speaker1: After the exam, a ton of posts about sex work pop up in the community.
Speaker2: So they’re thinking of selling themselves to get into college?
Speaker1: When a towel turns into a rag, it just becomes a mop in the end.
Speaker2: No matter how much you wash a rag, it's still a rag; schools should teach that.

Speaker1: Why is it so funny seeing influencers just in the rain? I crack up every time.
Speaker2: At first, it kinda bugged me, but now I’m just enjoying it like watching monkeys at the zoo.
Speaker1: Kinda worried they'll die young like that, so I guess I should lose some weight too.
Speaker2: I saw before that they died in their 30s. Gaining weight can clog your blood vessels and lead to a short life.

Speaker1: They say the drop in youth crime in the U.S. since then is because of the generation born after abortion was legalized.
Speaker2: So you're saying parents who raised kids without abortion are fools.
Speaker1: It seems like even though this country had a lot of female abortions 20-30 years ago, the antisocial issues for women haven't been solved and might've even gotten worse. I think a whip is the answer for beasts.
Speaker2: The 82-born Kim Ji-young generation, directly affected by female fetus abortions, definitely didn’t act like today’s women when they just became adults.

Speaker1: Looks like there are always warning signs before a big event. They just covered it up, and now dozens are dead.
Speaker2: This is just a crazy situation.
Speaker1: It's hilarious that the Korea Employers Federation was saying we don't need the Serious Accident Law in a situation like this.
Speaker2: It's ridiculous that they still say it's a tough country for businesses in situations like this.

Speaker1: Everyone's just itching to pounce when a newbie shows up, huh?
Speaker2: Guys' groups bully in their own way, and girls' groups do it too.
Speaker1: But seriously, not a single one of those turf-war people is legit.
Speaker2: It's just how the clueless communicate.

Speaker1: They say if we live to our life expectancy, 3 out of 10 people will get cancer.
Speaker2: Isn't that more like a cruel joke than a life expectancy?
Speaker1: What’s the point of a 100-year life when 80% of seniors in Korea are living in poverty?
Speaker2: I think we should introduce euthanasia here too. It’d be better to live as long as you want and leave when you want.
Speaker1: I think living long without quality doesn't mean much.

Speaker1: But if they can't drive for delivery or take taxis, how are they supposed to make a living? Getting a regular job's gonna be even tougher.
Speaker2: Isn't that obvious? How can you know what they'll do when the door's open?
Speaker1: Seriously, with all the crime out there, does it make sense to just target sexual offenses?
Speaker2: One criminal got caught. If you had a problem, you shouldn't have committed a sex crime.

Speaker1: I think senior zones are more profitable than kids' zones these days.
Speaker2: You not know about the old folks' coffee shop incident?
Speaker1: At least those folks still place orders.
Speaker2: It's frustrating that with the one-drink rule, they have to force themselves to drink when they're already full from coffee.
Speaker1: Yeah, that happens too. Like when four women and four kids come and only order one serving of tteokbokki. So annoying.
Speaker2: Old folks act like they’re at a café, just sitting there and asking why no one’s taking their order.

Speaker1: The subway difference between rich and poor neighborhoods in Seoul is huge.
Speaker2: Which areas in Seoul are you talking about? I'm curious if you've even used the subway there.
Speaker1: There's a huge difference from the escalators to the subway restrooms.
Speaker2: I wonder how hard life has to be to think like this.

Speaker1: I rushed my mom to the ER after she suddenly collapsed. Please pray for her, everyone.
Speaker2: Is there really time to post on social media in a situation like that? I don’t get it.
Speaker1: I just needed someone to pray. We're still waiting at the hospital.
Speaker2: Wouldn't it be better to put the phone down and pray for yourself in that situation?
Speaker1: You seem to be overreacting. Just go away and stop stirring things up.

Speaker1: Aren't kid cafes just accepting that stuff comes with running a kids' zone?
Speaker1: Sounds like they’re saying they wish they wouldn’t take kids in because it’s tough with them around.
Speaker2: Just live like that forever without complaining. It's all your fault if it's tough.
Speaker1: How about focusing on your own life instead of venting about some random person?

Speaker1: They should be fired and punished, not just have their resignation fixed!
Speaker2: So you’re saying don’t fix my resignation? That 250,000 won is just ridiculous.
Speaker1: They’re just trying to game the system for a pension; we should fire them and take that away.
Speaker2: Gotta get that pension even if you go to jail.

Speaker1: Looks like guys in the 2030s are making their lives way harder than they need to. Time to face reality and just accept it, I guess.
Speaker2: Honestly, it’s really annoying to lump all 2030 guys in with a handful of YouTube addicts or cult followers.
Speaker1: It's ridiculous to generalize all women just because one messes up when you claim it's a universal issue. So pathetic.
Speaker2: Guess those bright young folks had no choice but to act that way.

Speaker1: No way I'm renting to anyone in their 20s. They trash the place and do whatever they want. Families with kids are out too.
Speaker2: Are you talking about renting a cheap studio somewhere out in the sticks?
Speaker1: It's in the suburbs, but it's an apartment. Don't worry about anything that doesn't have good resale value.
Speaker2: You didn't take out a loan to buy it, right?

Speaker1: I think people who cut back on sleep just to be active are kinda frauds.
Speaker2: Not getting enough sleep messes with your judgment, makes you irritable, can lead to depression, and builds up fatigue that could eventually lead to dementia.
Speaker1: That "you gotta sleep less to succeed" stuff is just for students; during growth years, you need enough sleep for your brain to develop healthily.
Speaker2: Of course, even if I say this, parents will still be blinded by ambition and tell you not to sleep.

Speaker1: It's not a good look to be overly self-conscious after thirty.
Speaker2: For real, being self-aware is such a blessing.
Speaker1: If you don't change in your 30s, it's pretty much hopeless as you get older.
Speaker2: Gotta keep your head in the game, 'cause things can get ridiculous real quick.
Speaker1: Gotta be careful not to get cocky or stubborn just because you’ve got some life experience; that’s when you start acting like a know-it-all.

Speaker1: Hope the new hire's sharp.
Speaker2: Don’t expect too much from the MZ generation these days. If they can just understand what you’re saying, that’s a win.
Speaker1: Yeah, that friend on the other team couldn’t even answer the phone. Guess their mom did everything for them?
Speaker2: At least it’s good if mom doesn’t have to call just because the kid overslept.

Speaker1: I really hope I win the lottery. I hate being useless at work, but I bet my bosses can't stand me.
Speaker2: Everyone needs a settling-in period. You seem kinda anxious and always on edge.
Speaker1: I just don’t think working suits me. Feels like my only way to chill and eat is winning the lottery.
Speaker2: That mindset is why work isn’t going well for you.

Speaker1: Isn't this actor just adorable? Feels like they still have that childlike spirit, and their whole vibe is just so lovable.
Speaker2: Is it really childlike? Seems more like acting immature and making a scene.
Speaker1: Nah, it’s just part of the image management for the show.
Speaker2: Ugh, I couldn't do that even if you paid me. I'd just stick to a regular job. What a mess for someone over 30.

Speaker1: I don’t get why they even let you write reviews if they’re just gonna take them down.
Speaker2: Guess they just want only good reviews that help their business.
Speaker1: I tried dipping it in the sauce and mustard, but it still smelled so bad I couldn't eat it. I don't get what's wrong with leaving a review to help other customers.

Speaker1: I've been recording at the convenience store because of all the crazy customers.
Speaker2: Isn't it illegal to record without consent?
Speaker1: It's tough dealing with so many people who just look down on me 'cause I'm a convenience store worker.
Speaker2: For sure, you’ll deal with less unfair stuff.
Speaker1: I've used it a few times. The manager often sides with the customers without knowing what's really going on.
Speaker2: The world’s big and there are a lot of weird people out there.

Speaker1: Why do we say 'thank you' every time the waiter brings food?
Speaker2: It's just saying thanks for the service.
Speaker1: I don’t get why I should say thanks when I’m paying for my food. It kinda seems pathetic, honestly.
Speaker2: You're not wrong, but it's just better that way. Plus, it's kinda become a habit now.
Speaker1: Honestly, I'd rather have a robot bring the food. No need to see a stranger's face.

Speaker1: Who won the Nobel Prize in Literature this year?
Speaker2: Don’t say “our women.” That author won, not our women.
Speaker1: The reason Han men are obsessed with Japanese women is because they're optimized for a looks-obsessed culture. They got nothing in their heads.
Speaker2: Anyway, with that smile and natural face, what chance do Korean girls have? Even K-idols would be impressive, but it's a shame for sports.

Speaker1: Those people are really impressive.
Speaker2: Where are semiconductor engineers supposed to go?
Speaker1: Even if a semiconductor engineer gets laid off, they’ve got so much knowledge in electrical stuff that they can get certified and work as a contractor, living a better life than you.
Speaker2: Not many places for engineers, though. I don’t get how they think they’re irreplaceable.

Speaker1: That friend’s from South America.
Speaker2: Looks like a South American vibe for sure.
Speaker1: That's bold of you to say that to a guy who's not exactly a looker.
Speaker2: I’d probably wanna puke just looking at him.
